subject.title: Plugin install doesn't build native bindings — plugins with better-sqlite3 fail on Node 24 (ABI v137) with bindings file not found

question: Should OpenClaw keep managed plugin installs script-disabled and only add native-addon diagnostics, or should it introduce a trusted opt-in native rebuild contract for plugin installs?
rationale: The source evidence confirms why native bindings are skipped, but changing that behavior crosses the untrusted package lifecycle-script boundary and needs maintainer policy intent.

options.title: Keep scripts disabled; add diagnostics
options.body: Add install/inspect/runtime detection for native dependencies with skipped or missing build artifacts and show clear rebuild or plugin-publisher guidance without automatically running package lifecycle scripts.

options.title: Add trusted opt-in rebuild
options.body: Introduce a manifest or policy-gated native rebuild path for trusted packages only, with explicit security docs and focused upgrade tests.

options.title: Leave plugin-owned
options.body: Reaffirm that native addon rebuilds are plugin-owned and close or document this as unsupported, accepting that users may still see late generic runtime failures.

recommendation.title: Keep scripts disabled; add diagnostics
recommendation.body: Add install/inspect/runtime detection for native dependencies with skipped or missing build artifacts and show clear rebuild or plugin-publisher guidance without automatically running package lifecycle scripts.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the major managed npm install isolation work and is the strongest history signal for the install-policy tradeoff.
